title: La Cathédrale/Quotes
kind: 場所・ミッション・その他

lines: For vendor quotes and others, see the following:
Marie: "Keep your demons to yourself, Roathe! Lest you are once more goading me into a fight."
- Roathe: "Do not blame me. They are like kavats - drawn to the person they know they will annoy the most."
- Roathe: "Must you incessantly be the source of noise, Marie? I am trying to think."
Marie: "I know your wounds are precious to you, Lyon. But you should let me tend to them."
- Lyon: "When Lua wept, did Sol offer to sear those seeping eyes shut?"
Marie: "Careful with that tail, Devil, or I may tie a knot in it."
- Roathe: "And if you wake with a shaven head, Marie, you will know why."
Marie: "By Sol I bless the day and all its labours!"
Lyon: "By Lua I bless the night and all its respite!"
- Roathe: "By the Void I wish these two would shut up."
Marie: "Confession is good for the soul, Devil. What burdens you?"
Roathe: "Besides the leaden monotony of this wretched existence?"
- Lyon: "Your existence will cease one day, and that is a comfort to all of us."
Lyon: "Marie, this burden should have been mine alone. I never meant you to be dragged down with me."
- Marie: "'Dragged down,' he says! I would have followed you willingly into Hell, my brother!"
Lyon: "The Tenno have endured much. It is a blessing that we never saw the depravity of Orokin society with our own eyes."
- Roathe: "Oh, you could never have survived in our time. Your sanctimony would have fizzled like a teardrop on a hot coal."
Lyon: ""Lo, for all his pride the devil has fallen, and hears no more the caterwauling of his witches.""
Roathe: "Witches were said to kiss the Devil's arse. Would you care to, Marie?"
- Marie: "Je vais te BOTTER le cul, sale maudit!"
Lyon: "I pray these eyes will one day look upon Lua again."
Marie: "They will, Lyon. Remain constant and everchanging, just as she is."
- Roathe: "I know you two aren't exactly up on current events, but Lua is even more shattered than Lyon. Who only has one eye, by the way."
Roathe: "So valiant in the war against sin, and yet so obstinately determined never to commit any of their own. Whatever happened to 'know your enemy'?"
- Marie: "Our enemy whispers constantly in our ear, Devil. "
Roathe: "What's it like, knowing that we broke your deity open like an egg and gutted her for riches?"
Lyon: "Would that your words alone could cause me pain, Roathe. Though I understand why you seek to cause me strife, and I pity you for it."
Roathe: "The Indifference, while no god, is an enemy to be understood, like any other. Quantify it. Comprehend it. And then we can hurt it."
Marie: "Madden a beast with pain and it will know only rage, Devil."
- Lyon: "The devil only dreams of tormenting others. How true to type."
Roathe: "The pair of you think I have no conscience at all, no soul. Your arrogance amuses me."
Lyon: "What good is a conscience if it is never permitted to speak?"
- Marie: "The devil must humble himself before something greater than he, if he can come to recognize such a thing exists."
Lyon: "Why is it you spend so much time speaking with the Cavia, Roathe?"
- Roathe: "Hm? Why, they are the only intelligent souls in this dreary place, Priest."
Marie: "What do you hope to find at the bottom of this... Dark Refractory, Devil?"
- Roathe: "I seek that which was taken from me. The only god worth worshipping, Marie - knowledge."
Roathe: "I cannot tell who is more insufferably dull, Lyon. You or Albrecht's butler. Best be careful, or they might mistake you for that dusty furniture you've collected."
- Lyon: "Do not mistake my decision to withhold words for my inability to use them. It is called "restraint." Perhaps you should look into it."
Marie: "We should invite Monsieur Loid and the Cavia for Solstice celebrations, Lyon! I think it would be quite wonderful, non?"
Lyon: "You are right. I believe they might enjoy it."
Roathe: "Well, if you're asking my opinion, I would rather put a blade in my thigh."
Roathe: "I am so disappointed in how far this future has fallen. So... superstitious. Almost worse than these two relics of the past."
- Marie: "Hold still, Devil - I will make you a relic, yet."
Roathe: "One thing I will give that idiotic ingrate Albrecht and his experiments - the Void is terribly useful for finding ways to create endless amounts of... rooms. Too bad they doomed us all."
Marie: "Ça demanderait au moins le Néant pour faire place à quelque chose d'aussi grand que ta fierté, espèce de grosse bouse de vache!"
